originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: the 2024 Radchenko–Ramos Theorem 2 and §4.2 prove exact-zero H0 uniqueness for the same gap product, by a two-sided Poincare–Wirtinger contraction, but do not state a finite additive bound in both nonzero ℓ2 sample residuals. The new theorem adds a normed linear interpolation lemma for nonzero data, an automatic H0→weighted-L2 regularity upgrade, and explicit two-axis constants. The 2011 hyperbola HUP and 2022 finite periodic NUDFT work do not give this nonuniform reciprocal-transform residual estimate. Its method is very close to known techniques; search cannot certify absolute priority.
residual_risks: A general unindexed Banach-frame or perturbative HUP estimate might imply the same result; this is not a proof of global priority.
The main sampling lemma and two-inequality algebra are elementary; the original 2024 uniqueness proof uses the same key analytic mechanism, so novelty and value are narrow, not a new gap threshold.

Distributional definition of reciprocal transform in H0 must use the continuous representative justified by Radchenko–Ramos Proposition 2.2; the estimate is not an assertion for arbitrary ambiguous distributional extensions.
No sharpness of constants or critical αβ=1 extension is established.

value.rationale: The natural observation problem is noisy Fourier recovery of a density on a hyperbola from two separated nonuniform arms. Exact uniqueness of H0 functions gives no quantitative conditioning under nonzero measurement errors. This result provides a concrete two-channel ℓ2 residual-to-L2 stability inequality in an infinite-dimensional class, with explicit sensitivity to both upper and lower gaps and the subcritical margin 1−αβ, and proves a nontrivial automatic weighted-L2 regularity upgrade from the data. A future stability/inverse-problem analysis can use precisely this estimate; it is not valued for a new uniqueness threshold, optimal constants, formal verification or code. The proof is short and leverages standard interpolation, narrowing but not removing its independent utility.
residual_risks: It is a straightforward quantitative refinement of a known Poincare uniqueness mechanism; it gives no optimal stability rate.
Its applicability assumes global ℓ2 residuals on both full bi-infinite arms and uniform positive gap bounds, which can be restrictive for noise models.

limitations: Qualitative antecedent Radchenko–Ramos uses essentially the same Poincare contraction argument, so originality and value judgments are narrow and best of knowledge.
No claim of formal or expert validation, independent certification, numerical testing, sharp constants, or a critical endpoint estimate.
